verses.text: Send lambs to the ruler of the land, from Selah through the wilderness to Daughter Zion’s mountain.
At the Arnon crossings, the daughters of Moab will be like birds wandering around after their nest has been scattered.
Give us advice! See that justice is done! Make your shade as dark as night in the middle of the day. Hide the people who’ve been driven out. Don’t hand over anyone who’s on the run.
Let my outcasts stay with you! Give Moab somewhere to hide from the destroyer. The one who squeezes people dry will be finished, the wrecking will stop, and the oppressors will be gone from the land.
A throne will be set up in faithful love. Someone will sit on it in faithfulness in David’s tent. He’ll judge fairly, seek justice, and waste no time doing what’s right.
We’ve heard how proud Moab is. The arrogance, the swagger, the rage, all of it. Those big boasts amount to nothing.
So Moab will cry for Moab. Everyone will wail. Completely crushed, you’ll mourn for the raisin cakes of Kir Hareseth.

Heshbon’s fields are dying, and so is Sibmah’s vine. The rulers of the nations broke its best branches. They used to reach as far as Jazer and stretch into the wilderness. Its shoots spread far and went across the sea.
So I’ll cry with Jazer over Sibmah’s vine. I’ll soak you with my tears, Heshbon and Elealeh. The battle shout has come down on your summer fruit and your harvest.
All the joy and laughter have gone out of the fruitful fields. No singing or cheering in the vineyards. Nobody’s stomping grapes in the winepresses. I’ve put a stop to the shouting.
My heart hums like a harp for Moab. Deep inside, I ache for Kir Heres.
Moab can show up and wear himself out at the high place. He can go to his sanctuary and pray. It won’t get him anywhere.
That’s what the LORD said about Moab back then.
But now the LORD says, “Within three years, counted as carefully as a worker on a contract would count them, Moab’s glory will be disgraced along with its huge crowd. The few left will be weak.”
